issues.description: Deprecation message could point to the exact one-line replacement.
issues.detail: The warning text names contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr but doesn't show how to compose them when both are needed. A user replacing redirected(stdout=a, stderr=b) has to figure out the nested-with form themselves. One extra clause in the docstring ("use two nested with statements, or ExitStack") would close the loop.
The .. deprecated:: 4.3 block says "Use the stlib's" — should be "stdlib's". Small, but it lands in rendered docs. Worth fixing in the same commit.

review.summary: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE. This is the right move: delete a bespoke wrapper, defer to the stdlib filter that already does the job, and let composition (nested with-statements) handle the two-stream case. The data here is trivial — two file objects swapped on sys — and contextlib already expresses it cleanly, so the custom helper wasn't earning its keep. Two nits: the deprecation message should hand users the one-line replacement for the both-streams case, and "stlib's" is a typo. Otherwise this is exactly the kind of subtraction more libraries should do.
